title: Circus Act
text: Éclair spun her sword around in flashy little circles, while Crocodile Guy took the blows one after another, holding his axe in a rough, brawny stance.

When it was Crocodile Guy’s turn, he brought his axe down in a mighty swing that split the ground open, but Éclair dodged gracefully, flowing past him with a sweeping stroke of her sword that grazed along his scales as she slipped around to his back.
It was the kind of movement only possible in a performance built around spectacle, and the crowd watched on in hushed fascination, as if entranced.
Today, Panda’s grandfather and an old woman had also come out from the opposite side of backstage to hold a supporting sparring match.
Éclair and Crocodile Guy were putting on an especially flashy show so as to keep the audience’s eyes from wandering over there too much.
“Eclair-san and Shion really move well together, don’t they? Even with Shion having the advantage, nobody’s heckling.”
“It certainly makes for a good picture, I say. Just out of curiosity, is not getting heckled the bar for being allowed to perform?”
“Nope. In the end it just comes down to the human side winning, and everything else is left up to them. The fact that there’s no heckling just means the two of them are that good.”
“Huh…”

“By the way, I think the most popular act was Motoyasu-kun’s. Besides his sparring with Wolf, the way he gracefully dodged the Filolials’ all-out attack got so much applause it practically brought the house down.”
I shot Itsuki a sharp, self-satisfied look, pressing the space between my thumb and forefinger against my chin to show off, as if to say “I told you so, indeed.”
“……Is that so.”
I had already earned myself a place in the Performance Hall of Fame, I say!

“Over in Zeltoble, the act between Motoyasu-kun and Sadeena-san was the most popular one. Motoyasu-kun’s flashy use of fire and spear, and Sadeena-san’s not-to-be-outdone skill with lightning, made for a great combo. Plus, Sadeena-san’s got that heavyweight presence going for her.”
While we were talking, the sound of a gong rang out.
It seemed the sparring performance had come to an end.
It closed with Éclair emerging victorious over Crocodile Guy, cutting him down cleanly with her sword.
The defeated Crocodile Guy was carried off on a stretcher.
Of course, in reality he hadn’t taken any damage at all.
Back behind the stage, Éclair let out a groan, looking somewhat troubled.
“Hmm… It seems Shion has completely read through my swordsmanship. I’ll need to train harder.”
“That’s not really…”

“His eyes are keeping up with me perfectly. Even if it’s a set of moves he already knows well, it still stings a little. If anything, I’m the one breaking into a cold sweat, worried I might actually land a hit on him.”
“I’ll help you anytime you need.”
Now, we were supposed to be preparing for the next act, but…
“Hey! We’re going out there again?! Itsuki! You do it!”
“Sword Guy, you’re bad at giving up. Just get it over with quick.”
“Not happening.”
“Time for Keel-kun and Ama’s tightrope walk~”
Luna-chan was also standing by in her Filolial form, all set to go.
“C’mon, Itsuki! You’re good at climbing trees, so this should be a breeze for you, right? Didn’t you say you can glide even if you fall off the rope? Just fly off and escape!”
“Ren… you really don’t know when to give up, do you.”
“I already know how this ends, and I hate it. I’d rather die than become those guys’ laughingstock.”
“‘Rather die’—and what about me, huh?!”
“Now, now.”
“Enough talk, off we go, I say.”
“I don’t wanna!”
As Ren whined “no, no” like a stubborn child, I grabbed him by the scruff and hauled him out onto the main stage.
I tossed him up the ladder, and we were all set to go.
Well, without much trouble, I poked at Keel and Ren with my spear, then kicked them off partway through so Luna-chan could catch them.
It was a sort of intermission act, drawing scattered laughter and applause.
“Gyaaaaaah—”
With another fine reaction today, Ren fell toward Luna-chan and made his way back behind the stage.
There was plenty of laughter.
I quickly threw both hands up too, showing off as if to declare humanity’s victory.
Then the Filolial-samas came climbing up in their angelic forms.
The next act, the trapeze, was about to begin.
“Yaaay”
“And—hup!”
“Here I go~! I shall soar with grace~!”
Many Filolial-samas can’t actually fly, but they’re quite skilled at aerial control, so trapeze acts in the circus are right up their alley.
The audience was captivated watching the Filolial-samas soaring through the air.
Of course, the pig was up there too, flying and showing off along with the rest.
According to Father, there’s no real difference in popularity by species when it comes to the trapeze.
Meanwhile, a ring of fire had been set up on stage.
Father came out onto the main stage, bringing along Wolf, Rabbit Guy in his rabbit-beastman form, Rival’s parent, and even Filo-tan.
He was holding a whip in his hand.
“Grrrrr…”
Just as rehearsed, Wolf growled and prowled around the ring on all fours.
“Go!”
Father cracked the whip—snap!—and at the command, Wolf leapt through the burning rings one after another, with Rabbit Guy following behind.
“Gyau!”
Next came Rival’s parent.
“Kweh!”
Filo-tan also cleared the rings happily, though not to be outdone by Rival, she did it while doing a backflip.
Ah, the feathers growing from the top of Filo-tan’s head got a little singed with a crackle!
“Next up is…”
Father brought out some balls and set them on the heads of Wolf, Rabbit Guy, Rival’s parent, and Filo-tan, having them balance them.
“Everyone, please burn this into your memories~. Okay, ready—one, two, three, pose!”
“Vofuuuuu”
“Kyuuuu”
“Gyauuu”
“Kweh!”
All together, they stood up on two legs and struck their poses.
Somehow… Father was starting to look like one of those trainer guys running a sea lion show at an aquarium.
By the way, is Rabbit Guy’s cry supposed to be “kyu”?
Personally, I think “Death-pyon” would suit him better, death-pyon.
“And furthermore—”
This time, Father placed brooms on each performer’s forehead and had them balance those instead.
Every one of them balanced right on command, like well-trained monsters.
Their attitude seemed to say this much was nothing at all.
“Next up—”
This time, Father brought out some hoops.
He tossed the hoops to each of them one by one, having them catch them and slip them around their necks.
“Alright, alright, here we go with this one!”
“Kweh!”

This time he tossed a hula hoop, and Filo-tan caught it, spinning it around one leg, flicking it up, passing it to the other leg, repeating the motion, then leaping up to toss it back to Father with a nice pop.
Meanwhile, Father threw a big ball at Rival’s parent, then smoothly sent Filo-tan’s returned hula hoop flying over to Wolf, who spun it around his torso.
“Gyau”
Rival’s parent bounced the ball Father had thrown, keeping it up in the air, then tossed it to Rabbit Guy, who skillfully balanced it on his head.
No doubt about it—Father was clearly running this show exactly like some act he’d once seen at an aquarium.
Ah, I wish I could’ve joined in too, dressed up as a usaunny.
“Puu-poo”
And right behind them, Panda rode past on a unicycle, blowing a trumpet while juggling beanbags.
Things just kept getting livelier and livelier.
“Wow—”
“Yaaay!”
“Waaaaaah!”
“Kou, let’s sing and dance now~”
And so, as if signaling the next act, the angelic Filolial-samas cheerfully began to sing.
Apparently, singing the hymns established by Melromarc’s Three Heroes Church went over particularly well with the crowd, among other things.
As it turned out, Elephant, the conductor, joined in here too, appearing while blowing on a large trombone-like instrument.

This part of the show seemed to be a free-for-all where anything went as long as you looked cheerful, so it seemed Itsuki had taken the opportunity to hop up onto the main stage too, waving ingratiatingly as he bounced around the venue.
Following suit, Wolf, Crocodile Guy, Rival, Panda, and more of the circus crew came skipping out one after another, forming a big circle.

And just as the circus reached its liveliest peak, the music suddenly cut off, the lights went dark, and once everyone had returned backstage, Lazy Pig suddenly appeared standing center stage, bowing as if to announce the act was over, and the lights went out.
Applause and cheers broke out in scattered bursts… and then, with the show over, the audience trickled off toward home in twos and threes.
And so, this show came to an end.
By the way, sometimes the next performance would start after just a few hours’ break, but since this one had been held rather late, that was it for the day.
Everyone headed home looking like they’d had a wonderful time.
